items.t: Fairview is on the south shore of False Creek, stretching from Granville Island east to Science World, and south to Shaughnessy; it takes in all of False Creek South, South Granville north of 16th Avenue, the Granville and Burrard corridors and the Broadway spine between Clark Drive and Vine Street; exact boundary roads in City text: Not verified pass.

Where the condo stock concentrates: in three distinct pockets — the False Creek South waterfront (mostly City ground-lease stock, excluded below), the Fairview Slopes / West 7th–8th Avenue belt above the shore (Terraces on 7th, Manhattan West), and the Oak Street / Marpole Avenue edge toward Shaughnessy (Hycroft Towers, The Oaks).

Main streets: West Broadway, Granville Street, Burrard Street, Oak Street, Cambie Street, West 4th, 6th, 10th, 12th and 16th Avenues. Vancouver General Hospital anchors the area at 899 West 12th Avenue.

Transit: the Broadway Subway (Millennium Line Broadway Extension) is a 5.7 km extension with six stations; the Province states it will open in fall 2027, with South Granville Station and Broadway-City Hall Station serving the area's west end and Cambie edge.

The City owns about 80% of False Creek South. That single fact explains the area's tenure mix — 12 leasehold strata buildings, 7 co-ops and 6 rental buildings on City land per the City's October 21, 2021 presentation — and why "waterfront Fairview" and "freehold Fairview" are different markets.

Most False Creek leases expire in 2036 per the secondary guide — inside a standard 25-year mortgage horizon, which is why lenders and buyers discount the stock and why the remaining lease term, not the suite, is the first number to check.

Three heritage houses at 16th and Burrard are one townhome project. The Maguire (1913), Bayne (1919) and Elson (1919) residences were restored as Heritage: Sixteenth & Burrard — 12 homes total — and the City's November 14, 2017 hearing minutes record all three as designated protected heritage property, which binds future exterior work.

Hycroft Towers predates the strata era it now lives in. Completed in 1952 as a rental-era Art Deco tower (Semmens & Simpson), it is today Strata Plan VAS90 with 158 units — an early-plan strata whose documents reward a slow read.

South Granville's Gallery Row is in Fairview. The South Granville shopping district and its Gallery Row art galleries sit inside the local area north of 16th Avenue — the retail amenity base for the Slopes and Oak Street stock.

Firehall Library is the branch. Vancouver Public Library's Firehall Branch is at 1455 West 10th Avenue, and Charleson Park (999 Charleson Street) sits on the False Creek South shore — the two civic anchors for the waterfront stock.

items.t: Fairview is one of the City's 22 distinct local areas, in the central section of the city, running from Granville Island along False Creek to Science World, and south to Shaughnessy; the City page does not state a full set of boundary roads in text, and exact boundary roads are not verified from a City text source. The Broadway Plan area covering the northern part of Fairview runs between Clark Drive and Vine Street and 1st and 16th Avenues.

Nearby areas: Kitsilano to the west, Mount Pleasant to the east, Shaughnessy to the south, and Downtown across False Creek to the north. Search names inside the area: "Fairview Slopes" (the slope neighbourhood under the FM-1 district), "False Creek South" (the waterfront community inside the local area), "South Granville" (the shopping district at its west side) and "Granville Island."

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: the Fairview Slopes side streets off West 7th Avenue and West 15th/16th Avenues — Fairview Village and Marvista on West 7th, Tisdall Row on West 15th, and the Heritage project at 16th and Burrard — not on the Broadway/Granville arterial frontages, which are apartment and mixed-use strata. False Creek South's waterfront stock sits on City-held leasehold land and is excluded on tenure.

Main roads and transit: West Broadway, Granville Street, Burrard Street, Cambie Street and West 2nd Avenue serve the area, with the Granville, Burrard and Cambie bridges crossing False Creek at its north edge. The 99 B-Line runs from Commercial-Broadway Station to UBC via West Broadway, and route 9 serves Broadway to Alma Street; Broadway-City Hall Station (Canada Line) and Olympic Village Station (Canada Line) serve the east and north-east edges. The Broadway Subway — a 5.7-kilometre Millennium Line extension from VCC-Clark Station to Arbutus Street with six new stations — is stated by the Province to be on schedule to open in fall 2027, with its South Granville and Broadway-City Hall stations in and at the edge of Fairview.

Anchors: Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is inside the local area on the West Broadway corridor; Charleson Park, 999 Charleson Street, sits on the False Creek seawall in False Creek South; the Firehall Branch of Vancouver Public Library is at 1455 West 10th Avenue; the City names Granville Island and the South Granville shopping district, with Gallery Row, as the shopping areas in Fairview.

items.t: Form B diligence (all three counted strata complexes): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For Fairview Village (1982) and Marvista (1980), the depreciation report and rainscreen/envelope history are the core documents; listing-level pet/rental lines in are listing data, not bylaws.

Plans and heritage: the Broadway Plan covers Fairview's northern half (Clark Drive to Vine Street, 1st to 16th Avenues) around the Broadway Subway (opening fall 2027 per the Province). The Heritage project's three houses are designated protected heritage property (City hearing minutes, November 14, 2017) — designation binds future exterior work for any buyer of those homes, whatever the tenure proves to be.

items.t: Fairview was named by the CPR's land commissioner. The City states Fairview was named by CPR Land Commissioner L.A. Hamilton, whose survey established the numbered system of east-west avenues and named the cross streets after trees, and that the False Creek and Fairview Slopes area was a forest of fir trees before that survey.

The hospital is inside the area, not across a bridge. Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, sits on the West Broadway corridor inside the Fairview local area — part of why the Broadway medical corridor's strata stock carries a worker-buyer pool that pure residential areas do not.

A "townhouse" search here lands on three different tenures. Within a few blocks a buyer meets freehold strata (Fairview Village, Marvista, Tisdall Row), City-land leasehold (False Creek South) and a service-contract retirement apartment building (Terraces on 7th) — the word "townhouse" in a listing settles none of it; the Title to Land field and the Form B do.

The subway is a dated fact, not a rumour. The Province states the Broadway Subway is on schedule to open in fall 2027, with South Granville and Broadway-City Hall stations serving Fairview's West Broadway corridor — and the Broadway Plan already covers the area between 1st and 16th Avenues, so lots inside the plan area carry expectations the base zoning alone does not show.

Fairview Slopes lots (FM-1 District Schedule): the FM-1 schedule covers the Fairview Slopes and states its intent is to enhance the small-scale residential character of the neighbourhood by encouraging retention of existing houses and permitting new low-profile residential development; FM-1 permits single detached houses, duplexes, multiple dwellings and multiple conversion dwellings, with a maximum floor space ratio of 0.60 and no minimum site area stated in the schedule overview. These are schedule rules, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Southern-street lots (R1-1 District Schedule): residential lots in the southern part of the local area also fall under R1-1 — minimum site area 306 m² for a single detached house or duplex and for a multiple dwelling of 3 to 4 units (minimum frontage 10.0 m), 464 m² for 5 units (13.4 m) and 557 m² for 6 to 8 units (15.1 m); a multiplex of up to 6 units or up to 8 rental units is permitted, and a single detached house may include a secondary suite and a laneway house. The zone for a specific lot: Not verified.

Commercial / mixed-use frontage: C-3A covers the commercial mixed-use streets (Broadway, Granville and the other arterials) — arterial frontage is development-site ground, not house-lot ground, and is priced on the district schedule and the Broadway Plan, not on lot comparables alone.
Serviced position: homes here are on City water and sewer services; a 2026 utility dollar figure for a home in this area confirmed on a City source: Not verified.

ALR vs non-ALR: ALR land inside the local area: Not verified — no ALR parcel is confirmed, and no ALR percentage split is stated. ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission.

Historic lot fabric — built fabric, not offerings: the City states Fairview was named by CPR Land Commissioner L.A. Hamilton, whose survey established the numbered system of east-west avenues and named the cross streets after trees, and that the False Creek and Fairview Slopes area was a forest of fir trees before that survey. That survey fabric is the origin of the existing lot pattern — history, not a subdivision offering.

False Creek South — City-held land under ground leases, inside this local area: A purchase in False Creek South is a purchase of a leasehold interest (or a strata/co-op interest on leased land), never of the fee-simple land itself — do not price it against freehold Fairview lots.
This leasehold position belongs to False Creek South ground inside Fairview only; it is stated here because the ground is here, and it is not a position about any other area's waterfront.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Fairview

items.t: Zoning — Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 (City of Vancouver): the district schedules that govern Fairview land are FM-1 (Fairview Slopes — maximum FSR 0.60, no minimum site area stated in the schedule overview, intent of retaining existing houses and low-profile new development), R1-1 (southern streets — minimum site areas 306 m² / 464 m² / 557 m² by unit count, multiplex to 6 units or 8 rental units, secondary suite and laneway house with a single detached house) and C-3A on the commercial mixed-use streets. Confirm the district for the specific lot on the City's zoning map before pricing any potential.

Community plan / SSMUH position as the City states it: the Broadway Plan covers Fairview's northern half (Clark Drive to Vine Street, 1st to 16th Avenues) as the plan for new housing, jobs and amenities around the Broadway Subway, and the Broadway Subway is scheduled to open in fall 2027.

Floodplain diligence — the north-edge item: the False Creek shoreline along the north edge is inside the City's designated floodplain dataset, and the City's False Creek Coastal Adaptation Plan states the False Creek floodplain area includes False Creek South passing through Fairview along the south shore; land in the floodplain is subject to the Vancouver Building By-law Floodplain Standards and Requirements for setbacks and flood construction levels. Whether a specific parcel is in the floodplain: Not verified — check the parcel in the City dataset before subjects come off.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Fairview ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

Vancouver Empty Homes Tax — 3%, VANCOUVER ONLY, applies here: properties declared, determined or deemed vacant are subject to a 3% tax of the property's assessed value, levied on empty and under-utilized Class 1 residential properties in the City of Vancouver; most residential properties are not subject to the tax, including principal residences and homes rented out for at least six months of the year. Vancouver owners must submit an annual property status declaration; the 2025 Empty Homes Tax payment was due April 16, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after that date. A vacant Fairview lot or a house lot held empty carries this exposure in a way a New Westminster or Burnaby lot does not — the EHT is a City of Vancouver tax only.

The Slopes schedule has no minimum lot size — and that cuts both ways (FM-1): FM-1 states no minimum site area in its schedule overview and caps floor space ratio at 0.60, so a Slopes lot's potential is read off the FSR cap and the retention intent, not off a subdivision minimum — copying the R1-1 ladder (306 m² and up) onto a Slopes lot misstates both its buildable area and its split potential.

The street pattern itself is a CPR survey artifact: the City states the numbered east-west avenues and tree-named cross streets came from CPR Land Commissioner L.A. Hamilton's survey, over what was a forest of fir trees — the regular lot fabric a buyer sees on the southern streets is that survey, still legible in the parcel pattern.
